column1: # tests/skip_tests.tsv — the NAMED exclusions from tests/run_all_tests.sh.
# #417, map #450. `bash tests/run_all_tests.sh` named 412 of the 744 scenes under
# `tests/` on trunk `6a25e54f7`. 300 of the other 332 emitted PASS/FAIL markers and
# were reachable by no runner at all. Some of them SHOULD be excluded. The defect
# was never the exclusion — it was that an unlisted test and a deliberately-skipped
# test are indistinguishable, so a test that silently stopped being run looks
# exactly like a test that was never meant to run. Both are "absent from an array".
# This file is where that difference gets a name on it, and
# `tools/check_test_list_coverage.py` is what makes writing it unavoidable: every
# scene under `tests/` must be listed in the array, declare `[NOT_A_TEST] <why>` on
# `tests/lib/verdict.sh`'s own channel, or have a row here.
# FORMAT: stem <TAB> class <TAB> reason. Three fields, tab-separated, no more.
# The class vocabulary is CLOSED and lives in the guard, with a paragraph on each:
#   red · environmental · broken · rig · slow · superseded · stranger
# A new KIND of exclusion is a decision and should cost a code change, not a word
# typed into a data file by whoever is in a hurry.
# THE REASON IS PROSE A HUMAN WROTE, and it has a job: six weeks from now it is the
# only thing standing between "we decided this" and "nobody noticed". A `red` row
# names the ticket holding the finding. A `slow` row carries the measured seconds.
# A `superseded` row names the successor. A `stranger` row names the rig that runs
# it, and that rig is what has to be green.

ADR-0194 dec. 7's engine arm. Boots STOCK Godot and asserts the fork's compositor primitives are ABSENT, so a `fork` declaration in plugin.cfg is a checked fact and not a note. Shared by every fork-declared rig; run by tests/stranger/<addon>/run.sh.

ADR-0194's baseline arm — the staged addon stands up in a project that did nothing for it. One implementation for every rig; the subject comes from the staged project's own name. Cannot run here: it asserts what happens WITHOUT this project. Run by tests/stranger/<addon>/run.sh.

ADR-0194 — the other half of the burn-down arm: loads the files a rig DECLARES not to compile in a stranger project and asserts each still fails, so a paid-off row cannot sit there describing a fixed file. Cannot run here: in the host they all compile. Run by tests/stranger/<addon>/run.sh when that rig has a known_failures.tsv.

ADR-0229's viewer arm — `SequenceViewer` comes up in a project with no sprite content and REFUSES in the words `exmateria_sprite_rig/content_root` names, without throwing. Cannot run here: `godot-learning/project.godot` always declares that setting, so the empty-content branch this scene exists to take is unreachable in the host and the arm's own precondition check would fail it. The first rig-owned scene in this family. Run by tests/stranger/exmateria_sprite_rig/run.sh.

ADR-0238's engine-fact arm — a `global uniform` a project has not declared in `[shader_globals]` is validated ONLY under `Engine::is_editor_hint()`, so outside the editor it compiles silently and reads its type's zero. Cannot run here: `godot-learning/project.godot` declares all seven names, so the arm's own anti-vacuity check would fail it in the host — which is the check working. Goes RED ON GOOD NEWS: if a future engine validates outside the editor, `check_addon_portability.py` arm 4 becomes enforceable. Run by tests/stranger/exmateria_platform/run.sh.
